principle_1_sign_of_priority_is_the_shed.name: One signed integer decides both rank and expendability
principle_1_sign_of_priority_is_the_shed.summary: A single per-workload priority both orders the queue (bands served highest first) and defines the refusal rule: negative means droppable under load, non-negative means the router will queue or serve it but never refuse it for load. The rule is defined once, in a two-line helper, and reused by admission, by the deadline admitter and by the in-flight eviction filter.
principle_1_sign_of_priority_is_the_shed.tradeoff: Crisp, auditable and impossible to make inconsistent across subsystems; but it is a cliff edge with no gradation, it conflates importance with urgency, and a fleet of all-default traffic has no refusal valve at all.

principle_2_exactly_one_terminal_outcome.name: Every queued request is finalised exactly once and the caller always learns why
principle_2_exactly_one_terminal_outcome.summary: Ownership of a queued item is passed explicitly between the distributor and the shard worker under a documented contract that whoever holds it must finalise it exactly once; a sweep every second reclaims anything finalised out of band. Each terminal state maps to a distinct caller-visible status: dispatched, capacity rejection, deadline expiry, client disconnect, internal error.
principle_2_exactly_one_terminal_outcome.tradeoff: Requests are never silently lost and back-pressure is honest, but the ownership protocol is intricate, needs a periodic sweeper, and tolerates short-lived stale entries that still occupy capacity.

principle_3_hard_exclusion_then_soft_ran.name: Separate what must not be used from what is merely preferred
principle_3_hard_exclusion_then_soft_ran.summary: Placement is two stages: filters remove disqualified endpoints, then scorers express graded preference as a weighted sum whose terms are each clamped into the unit interval so no single signal can dominate. The filter chain short-circuits the moment it empties, and the shipped weights encode the view that cache locality outranks queue depth and memory pressure.
principle_3_hard_exclusion_then_soft_ran.tradeoff: New signals can be added without touching the others and a buggy one cannot hijack the decision; but the clamp flattens genuinely extreme signals, and a hard filter discards information the scorers could have used to pick the least-bad option.

principle_4_treat_unobservable_as_unusab.name: Stale state is worst-case for refusal and disqualifying for routing, yet the filter fails open
principle_4_treat_unobservable_as_unusab.summary: An endpoint whose telemetry is older than 200 ms contributes a full saturation score when deciding whether to refuse, and is dropped from the routing candidates. But if that rule would eliminate every endpoint, the unfiltered list is returned instead, so placement can never starve for lack of candidates.
principle_4_treat_unobservable_as_unusab.tradeoff: Deliberately conservative where a wrong guess would overload a blind endpoint, deliberately optimistic where refusing everything would be worse than trying; the cost is that a fleet-wide telemetry outage degrades silently into load-blind routing, and the behaviour is asymmetric with the per-profile filter chain, which fails closed.

principle_5_serialize_the_decision_shard.name: Make each capacity decision a single-writer transaction, then scale by running many of them
principle_5_serialize_the_decision_shard.summary: All state-mutating operations on a queue shard run on one goroutine, which makes the capacity check and the enqueue atomic without locks; throughput is recovered by running independent shards and sending each arrival to whichever shard currently holds the least of that workload's backlog, with a non-blocking pass across all shards before a single blocking submit provides back-pressure.
principle_5_serialize_the_decision_shard.tradeoff: Capacity accounting is exact and lock-free and the system degrades into back-pressure rather than overcommit; but per-shard accounting means global limits are only approximately enforced, and each shard is a serial bottleneck whose input buffer is the only shock absorber.

principle_6_policy_is_configuration_not_.name: Every behavioural choice is a named, swappable plugin with an injected default
principle_6_policy_is_configuration_not_.summary: Ordering, fairness, saturation detection, usage ceilings, pickers, scorers, filters and the body parser are all plugin references resolved from a registry; the loader injects a default for any role the operator left empty, so the system is always structurally complete without hard-coding a policy. That makes the strongest opinions explicit defaults rather than assumptions.
principle_6_policy_is_configuration_not_.tradeoff: One deployment can be retuned from greedy-global to strictly fair, or from throughput-first to deadline-first, without a rebuild; but the shipped defaults are what most operators actually run, so a default like the globally greedy fairness policy silently means no tenant isolation.

principle_7_randomize_ties_accept_nondet.name: Break ties by chance rather than by list order
principle_7_randomize_ties_accept_nondet.summary: A process-wide generator seeded from the wall clock shuffles candidates before the stable sort, powers the weighted and uniform pickers, and picks among equally weighted rewrite targets, so equal-ranked options receive equal traffic with no coordination.
principle_7_randomize_ties_accept_nondet.tradeoff: Eliminates systematic concentration on whichever endpoint happens to be listed first and needs no shared state; but it makes placement unreproducible on replay, untestable by exact comparison and unexplainable after the fact, and the seed is never exposed for pinning.
